newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar falls under $300 as spread sold.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar falls under $300 as spread sold.

text.p: London's March white sugar contract drifted back under the key $300 barrier on Monday as commission house March/May sales countered the effect of earlier broker shortcovering.
But nearby values were pinioned in tight ranges and a lacklustre performance on the raws market failed to inspire much business on the white premium.
March/May narrowed to $1.50 from $2.00 earlier in the session and the third-month August contract firmed gently to bring May/August into contango.
At 1620 GMT March stood 40 cents lower at $299.90 after hitting an intraday high of $301.40. May was down 20 cents at $298.40 but the further forwards which were traded gained slightly.
Overall volume totalled 1,515 lots although some 600 lots of this was reported to derive from agaainst actuals trades.
Earlier, broker liquidation of short March positions in the little time remaining before next week's spot expiry accounted for most of the volume.
There was little activity on the March/March arbitrage, with trade sellers waiting above the market to cap any gains, although light interest was noted in the May premium at around $69.
Technical analysts said March's 40 day moving average would provide resistance at just over $302.00 with support at $298.30, the upward trendline dating from mid-January.
Prices were likely to head higher in the short term but there were doubts momentum would be enough to pierce the $312.80 high seen early last month.
All traded positions were lower on the Paris market in a volume of 1,476 lots.
March was down $1.00 at $299.20 and May down 70 cents at $298.50.
